utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Crispian Smith and Selma Sakic for the Prosecution this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Stanisic's Defence team, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, Aleksandar Aleksic, and Jason Antley, appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. We're grateful to the parties for their indulgence in terms of the late start this morning the reasons for which will become patent in a moment, but that will be in private session. Is there any matter to be dealt with in open session before we --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two matters. One which will have to be dealt with in private, because it relates to the witness, and the second matter, however, is one which we're delighted to be able to tell Your Honours about. After discussions with the Defence, you will recall we asked for a witness summons for a particular witness who was going to cover adjudicated fact 928. That was Witness 250. And I'm delighted to say that both Defence teams will stipulate to that adjudicated fact as originally written without the crossings out. So it will read, perhaps just for the record: "Enver Burnic, a Bosnian Muslim former policeman, was taken outside the Betonirka factory garages on St. Vitez Day, 28th of June," should be 1992, "by shift commander Martic, a Bosnian Serb policeman who was drunk, and by two policemen and beaten. He was told at the time that a bullet was too costly a way for him to die." So that is the full adjudicated fact which the Defence will stipulate to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, do we understand now that now that is an agreed fact?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. By stipulation I mean -- that's actually an American term, but I would put it as an agreed fact. So that's the first [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic [sic] nodding --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- so it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Mr. Krgovic is also nodding. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence has been trying all this time to find a way to save Their Honours time by agreeing on facts. Therefore, we have stipulated to this fact together with the Prosecution. We will continue work on this, but it will take a while. It is not just the matter of looking at facts and the underlying evidence. Rather, since these are facts from a different case, we have to look into what other witnesses testified to on these same events, and that's why it makes it difficult for us to stipulate to certain facts right away. We want to make sure that the event really played out the way it is described in the adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We appreciate the effort, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, a second agreed fact -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the position --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, before we -- let's finish dealing with this matter. The position at bottom is that the subpoena -- the application for subpoena is withdrawn in respect of 250.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we now have that on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second agreed fact is 564. We filed a motion on the 8th of October to add Witness ST-016 to cover that fact. That is also now going to be an agreed fact and will read as follows: "On 10th of July, 1992, Bosnian Serb special police and soldiers in JNA uniforms rounded up Bosnian Muslim men and women from the Biljani hamlets at the local school building." And that's now also an agreed fact by both parties. So, again, our application for -- to add ST-016 is withdrawn. And if perhaps both Defence parties again could confirm that this is now agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I can confirm this. We had contacts with the Prosecution yesterday about this adjudicated fact. Another matter. In order for us to review all the adjudicated facts and the underlying documentation, unless we manage to do it after this witness's testimony, we may require one or two working days next week to review these facts. I will be able to give you a definite position tomorrow. These two days would help save us at least 15 to 20 court days in general. So this afternoon we will look into the various facts and see how much time we need to review them, and this will substantially reduce the time of testimony required for these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic is asking for two days off, in other words, not to call a witness. It's a bit late because we've got witnesses lined up and we really can't unwind them. So, you know, even if it takes three afternoons or whatever, we'd still prefer -- in any event it is only a four-day week next week because of the holiday on Monday. So, I'm sorry, I mean as much as we'd like to get some agreement, we do have witnesses lined up for the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could get a list of these witnesses and deal with them first, and then -- or, rather, focus on those who would be coming up later on so we have time enough to decide not to call them. Again, I repeat, these are thousands, upon thousands of pages of testimony of these witnesses in other cases. We are simple physically unable to go through them all and analyse them thoroughly. We do have a duty toward our clients to defend them appropriately wherever possible. Matters that are quite obvious and evident can be agreed to right away. Others have to be looked into. And let me just add, these adjudicated facts we've stipulated to are the results of precisely such work. I will be able to come up with a full proposal next week because I don't want to make promises I will not be able to keep.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said, Mr. Krgovic's got Monday anyhow. And the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, but I nevertheless think that it would be helpful if we could be provided, and the Defence, of course, with the list of witnesses for next week and the week thereafter. Some sort of planning possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, we can certainly do that. We know exactly who is coming next week. I'm not entirely sure about the week after, but I will check that with Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I had indicated when we started that the Judges' own work in the 15 minutes before we took the Bench, we would have been reporting on but having regard to what counsel have indicated, we may or may not have to speak to what we had -- the path that we were suggesting and we're going to look at it again in the course of today, and, if necessary, we will deal with this later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, before the witness comes in, can we go into private session, in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. Before Mr. Krgovic resumes his cross-examination, I remind you you're still on your oath. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we left off discussing the events surrounding Kotor Varos. I won't be using maps now. Can you tell me, the information you had in June of 1992, the intelligence you had, did it indicate that the Muslim/Croat forces had practically Kotor Varos under their control in some sort of an encirclement?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intelligence available to me at the time - and, of course, I don't have the relevant documents with me here - indicated that the municipality of Kotor Varos was a conglomerate of localities permeated by tensions which had existed from before. The fact of the matter is that there were all sorts of political colours represented, and, by the same token, military formations in the various villages. That's why one could say that even the urban core of Kotor Varos found itself in some sort of an encirclement, in respect of these rural areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You will have been aware of the fact that before the clashes in Kotor Varos broke out, these formations would block roads, either in the direction of Teslic or in the direction of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These were stories I heard, nothing that I or my unit saw. I suppose other witnesses could give you more thorough information on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to the Prosecutor's question in September earlier this year, you recognised Slobodan Dubocanin in a piece of footage shown to you by the Prosecutor, if you remember. If I remember correctly, Slobodan Dubocanin wore a uniform that was not your typical JNA or VRS uniform but it bore the insignia of armoured mechanised units, did it not?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a still where I recognised Slobodan Dubocanin. I met him on a couple of occasions, and he introduced himself to me. In the footage, I was not able to see any insignia of his officer's rank or the armoured mechanised units. However, I stated, and I stand by that, that sometime in September or October he came to see me because he wanted to report to the brigade in Knezevo. At that time he had the rank of a lieutenant, and he also had a tank on his patch, which stood, of course, for the armoured mechanised units. That was when I saw his insignia, not before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, you did not pay particular attention to that, nor did you see him that often, to be able to recognise the insignia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't pay attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution asked you about a special unit, although it was not within your area of responsibility, as you rightly put. Do you know that, in fact, there were two types of special units in Kotor Varos; namely, one, from the CSB Banja Luka; and the other which was under the direct command of Mr. Stevilovic and directly subordinated to General Talic?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I'm hearing this. I know that the unit -- I know about the unit from the CSB of Banja Luka. Milan Stevilovic was a colonel, chief of security of what was by then already the 1st Krajina Corps. I don't know that he had a unit of his own. I had never heard anything like this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's been put as though there's been evidence to this effect. And unless I'm very much mistaken, I don't believe there has been any evidence to this effect. I'm sorry, can I just repeat, I do -- it's the form of the question again. It shouldn't be put as though this is an established fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will recall that there was evidence of this type before the Chamber, and I just wanted to know if the witness was aware of this. I don't want to name the witness who testified on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, inasmuch as the recollection of counsel differ on this point, I -- I'll allow Mr. Krgovic to proceed. But, of course, you remember to phrase the question in such a way that you aren't telling the witness on the stand what another witness has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question for the witness was whether he was aware of it. I didn't suggest that there was. And now since the Prosecutor objected to the form of the question, I wanted to say that there was a witness who testified to this effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, was Colonel Stevilovic present at the time - that's to say, in the summertime - in Kotor Varos; and was he killed in one of the ambushes in the area?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Stevilovic came to the area two or three times. I can't be sure. It's been a long time. He definitely did come, and I suppose it was his call of duty and as ordered by his superior, General Talic. My understanding was that he was to look into the situation in general, in terms of security, and, on one occasion, he talked to a group of people in order to ascertain what the situation was like in the village of Vecici. The objective was to find a solution once and for all to reduce tensions. From what I was able to see, his efforts were directed at easing tensions and making sure that people were able to live together. So he was supposed to intermediate between the leading structures in the village of Vecici and the authorities in Banja Luka. So, yes, Colonel Stevilovic was there two or three times, from what I knew. Yes, in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Stevilovic was chief of security of the 1st Krajina Corps; is that right? Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was chief of security in the 1st Krajina Corps. And up the chain of command, he was directly subordinated to the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After his death, Colonel Bogojevic replaced him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the assassination of Colonel Stevilovic, Stevo Bogojevic replaced him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, in July, shortly after the assassination of Mr. Stevilovic, Stipo Maric, aka Sprzo, was killed. I think there was a name you mentioned yesterday as well.

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There was an action with members of the MUP when the name by the nickname of Sprzo was killed. It was a group of people - I don't know how many; I didn't look into that - that was when I heard that Stipe Maric, aka Sprzo, was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, he was definitely unable to take part in the negotiations about disarming in Vecici in September and October later that year? And I'm referring to Maric.

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. A dead man cannot engage in negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show to the witness P1502.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report drafted by a MUP officer, MUP of Republika Srpska, who toured or visited the CSB in the area and who's talking about the special detachment and the meeting. You are certainly aware that at certain points the units of this police special detachment had been put at the disposal at the 1st Krajina Corps under the direct command of General Talic. Would you please take a look at the last sentence that we can see on this page. Here it is stated that the police special detachment, its strength being 100 members, is placed under the command of General Talic in the 1st Krajina Corps, as of 10th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the following page of the document in the B/C/S put up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We see here that the handover of the unit will be carried out on the 10th of August in Kotor Varos where the unit is deployed. The handover will be attended by Djuro Bulic, SJB sector chief on behalf of the CSB, and by Colonel Bogojevic, military security chief on behalf of the 1st Krajina Corps. Sir, were you aware then that the 1st Krajina Corps or, rather, Colonel Bogojevic took up the authority and command over this unit that they were integrated into the VRS, or, rather, into the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that. I did not attend the handover. I see the document for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to Mr. Dubocanin, I would like to ask 2D56 to be put up on the screen for the witness. Could we please zoom in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is Slobodan Dubocanin's file, his personnel file.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we please see page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the right segment of the document, we can see what his status was. Lieutenant, and then captain, as of 11 -- no, 20th of November,

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, all this has been in open session. Mr. Krgovic, all this is in open, and the answers ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tried to be careful in my questions. I spoke about the witness just being part of a brigade. I didn't mention what his function was or rank. Maybe the answers of the witness would identify him. Maybe it would be good to have this redacted. But I think my questions were such that it was not possible to identify the witness. We never mentioned his position or anything else. A brigade has 2.000 troops so ... I believe that this line of questioning cannot jeopardise the identity of the witness, but if you feel it should be done, we can redact it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: There was earlier on a question that was -- which the Court Officer was alert to and that was redacted. But I agree with Mr. Krgovic. Unless I'm missing something, I don't think that any of the recent questions would have identified the witness. Unless, of course, Ms. Korner, your concern was about the personal records of somebody -- of the individual who the subject of the present line of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, so we'd redact that line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And all of the discussion that we've now had, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Answering to the Prosecutor's questions, you were shown also a series of documents about your presence at the meetings of the Crisis Staff where Mr. Djokanovic was also mentioned. Outside of the sessions or meetings, did you have an opportunity, maybe at some picnic or during a lunch somewhere out in the open, did you have an opportunity to spent some time with Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Djokanovic on several occasions. Mr. Djokanovic also came to visit troops in Slavonia also, because some of the troops from the 122nd Brigade were from the Kotor Varos municipality. And, yes, therefore, I did meet with him on two or three occasions when he came to visit us in Slavonia. And not only him. Some other municipal presidents as well. It was an established practice that people from local authorities, primarily presidents of municipalities and the municipality Executive Boards, as it was called at the time, that they would come and tour the units. Now, whether I've ran into him at some picnic -- well, I don't know. It was a time of war, not a time of picnics. We may have met somewhere, but I cannot tell you when or where. It may have happened that we have had lunch and that he came along. I really don't remember. I may have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then you probably wouldn't remember whether you attended a lunch where Mr. Stojan Zupljanin was present as well as Mr. Slobodan Zupljanin and Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember anything of the sort. It may have happened but it was 18 years ago. I have difficulty sometimes remembering what happened yesterday, let alone 18 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I guess then you don't remember a conversation between Mr. Djokanovic and Mr. Zupljanin about events in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for not switching on my mic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The OTP asked you a series of questions related to the town defence command. They showed you a document. These were the minutes of a Crisis Staff meeting that was held in Kotor Varos where there's mention of the town defence command. Although that was not part of your area of responsibility, were you familiar with the fact that during a period because of the war, commands of the town defence was formed in the spirit of the JNA regulations?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise in advance, but I will have to give you a longer answer because it is obvious that may have misunderstood this phenomena of town defences and what transpired in the conversations with the OTP. In peacetime, JNA had town defence commands -- or, rather, city defence commands that referred only to cities. Sometimes they were called commands of the Military District or garrisons and for a while they were called city defence commands, but that applied to Belgrade, Zagreb, Ljubljana, Sarajevo and such garrisons which had more comprehensive civilian and military functions. So that is one phenomena, and I'm explaining the regulations. Another phenomenon of the town defences is something that you can find in the tactical and defence rule-books where there is description of town defences when towns are in the zone of defence of a tactical combat unit. The third thing, and that was presented to me in a document signed by General Pujic in late 1991 about establishment of civilian affairs organs that were to take up carrying out some activities and also be active in town defence duties within former SFRY, and I answered that this document never took effect, because one cannot talk about crisis areas within SFRY at a stage where two republics have already seceded from it. I was also shown a document where either in Gornji or Donji Vakuf the command of the 19th Brigade had established a town defence command, and the document bore the stamp of the 19th Partisan Division or, rather, Brigade. That was a JNA brigade. And in my response, I said it was an improvisation because such a stamp was not legal anymore. I was shown this document by the War Presidency of Kotor Varos where one can see that town defence command was established in Kotor Varos, and whereby Mane Tepic was appointed either a commander or some kind of officer - I don't have the document in front of me - I have heard of that only when I was reading this document. I don't know that Mane Tepic was the commander of the town defence and why would he be, when the town included the command of the 1st Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade? Because, according to rules of combat for the brigade, the commander of a military unit where the town is is automatically commander of the town defence. But I'm talking about defence in the tactical sense, not defence as an organ or an institution. So, yes, I've seen that in this document, but I really don't know that Mane Tepic was or was not commander of any defence, for how long, what his duties may have been. What I do know is that before the conflict broke out, Mane Tepic was the commander of the municipal Territorial Defence Staff. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document 1510 [as interpreted]. It's a 65 ter document. It's number 34 in the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I said 65 ter 10510. Can we please zoom in the Serbian version? This is a document, it's an excerpt of the minutes from the Crisis Staff meeting of 28th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, it's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In item number 1 -- and yes, can we please move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to delay the witness coming back in again, but I think all sides, in particular, the Defence for Mr. Zupljanin, would welcome Your Honours' input on timings for the next week. Your Honours, at present, we have three witnesses next week to deal with adjudicated facts. The fourth witness no longer applies, because we've just had the -- the agreed fact that Witness 250 was going to testify to agreed. The following week, all of the witnesses are to do with adjudicated facts. So our suggestion would be, at present, we can fill next Friday by bringing up another witness. But it occurred to us that it may help if we had not only the Monday off, but the Tuesday off, and by then we -- but only on the basis that the Defence teams of whom there are numerous members, as Your Honours will have seen, can get to grips with the adjudicated facts and tell us, finally, which ones they are prepared now to agree. So instead of bringing up a witness to fill Tuesday to Friday, we would simply move back the three witnesses, one of them, ST-225, is actually quite lengthy because it is an all-encompassing adjudicated fact to do with the events in Banja Luka. So we've asked for three hours in-chief for him. So that's our suggestion. Now, I don't know whether that finds favours with Your Honours, or we were in the middle of a rather animated and inconclusive discussion about this, but that's our suggestion because we really need to know whether any of the adjudicated-fact witnesses who are coming the week of the 1st of November can be dispensed with. And I'm raising it now so that we can try and get an answer before the end of today's session. Your Honours, sorry, there's one other matter. I'm so sorry to interrupt, but, obviously, from the point of view of planning, we need to have a ruling as soon as possible from Your Honours about the witnesses we've applied to call under the 92 bis procedure but which -- to which the Defence have objected. Because if Your Honours rule that they must come, then they will be added in as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose I can say that ruling is imminent. Is the -- Ms. Korner's first point about the efficient use of next week, are there any observations which the Defence would wish to add; or is this something that your, quote/unquote, animated discussions would continue and we would probably, at the beginning of the next session, get a clearer idea as to where you stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We have ongoing discussions with the Prosecution. Before taking a final decision, we, the Defence teams, need to meet up and take up a joint position. Now I have to focus on my cross-examination, but over the next break, I will check and go through all the witnesses that Ms. Korner has just referred to so that we can give you our position at the end of work today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course, today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Today being Wednesday, if the next break is -- puts too much pressure on you, we could be informed in the usual manner in the course of -- by the -- later in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I don't want to be difficult about this, but we have to start making arrangements and in particular if we're going fill the Friday slot, because the -- the Defence say that -- that -- that they cannot give us the definitive answer, then we need to get that in train this afternoon. So, if necessary, Your Honours could perhaps take, instead of 20 minutes, 25 minutes to allow the Defence -- it is really not a difficult problem, this, whether they want the extra day and will come with a final decision, or don't. It's as simple a question as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- we appreciate Ms. Korner's concern about the urgency of this matter, but we -- we think that the -- if necessary, that the Defence should be allowed the extra few hours to deal with this at a point later than the -- during the final session. But if at all possible, we would wish to be in a position to rule on this matter during the third session today. Reverting to the matter with which we opened this morning, the Chamber has an observation to make, and that is as follows. The Trial Chamber welcomes the ongoing discussions between the parties to try to reach agreement as to stipulations. The positive effect that these discussions can have is amply demonstrated by the withdrawal of the two applications this morning. The Trial Chamber reminds the parties that it has no formal notification of the nature or scope of any of the stipulations already agreed or under discussion. This has raised concerns about the impact that they may have on other aspects of the case, in particular, the five recently filed motions for admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis and quater. The Trial Chamber therefore directs the parties, first, to file with the Chamber, no later than Friday of this week, a notice setting out in full the stipulations that have already been reached, for example, in relation to events in Visegrad. Second, the Trial Chamber informs the parties that it will not address those Rule 92 bis and quater applications in respect of which the Defence has raised issues relating to possible stipulations while those discussions are still ongoing. In the interim, the Prosecution is directed to schedule the affected Rule 92 bis witnesses as viva voce witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I hear what Your Honours say on this matter. In fact, I'm rising to my feet not because of that but because of something that I raised with Mr. Krgovic; namely, when he put to the witness that there was a special unit in Kotor Varos under the command of Colonel Stevilovic, totally separate from the police special unit, in the interim I asked Mr. Krgovic, because, as I said, I could not recall any such evidence being given in the case, where that evidence came from, he stated to me that it came from a witness, I cannot remember his number now but he gave me the name, and we've checked that and there is no such reference. Now, Your Honour, I'm raising this because it's not the first time, and I know how difficult it is when one is on one's feet to give accurate quotation, that assertions are being made to a witness as though this was evidence in the case. And, as I say, I would remind -- I would ask Your Honours to remind Mr. Krgovic that the form of the question is important because we've seen before witnesses take it for granted that what counsel says is a fact, is a fact and may agree to it. And so I -- I would ask that the questions are phrased properly as questions and not as assertions of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. I don't know that we need add anything. It is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: A question should never be promised -- premised on facts not in evidence or, I suppose, by extension, in respect of which the party raising it is in no position to lead evidence at some future point. So parties should remember that. Could we have the blinds down so the witness may be escorted back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I may have explained to you on a previous occasion that the nature of a trial involves not only receiving testimony from a witness but often entails having to deal with procedural issues. So to the extent that you were inconvenienced by being kept waiting for longer than you expected is one of those unavoidable incidents of a trial. Mr. Krgovic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we broke off while we were discussing the town defence command. You said that, if I understood you correctly, the OTP had shown you a document coming from the 19th Partisan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 2D02-1954.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the document you were shown by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This order by the commander, we can see that the town of Donji Vakuf command was being established, consisting of, and we see who were in the command. Jovetic Milan, reserve captain. And then Bosko Savkovic, this is what I am interested in, who has been conscripted, is appointed chief of the Donji Vakuf public security station. Also a council of the Donji Vakuf municipality is also being appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the following page of the document presented on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Under 3, or in item 3 of this order, the organs for state administration are being formed, including the judiciary, the education staff, then economic organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the following page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We can see organs for public utilities are formed for special functions and information of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we now please have the last page of the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Item 4, the commander, this lieutenant-colonel, appoints the president and judge of the municipal misdemeanour court, Mr. Miodrag Jandric. And 5, he appoints for the commander of the Donji Vakuf public security station, I think the proper name is Sekula Sisic, who is captain first class, and both his deputy and his assistant. In my understanding of this order, the commander of this military unit appoints or puts under control all elements of the authorities in this municipality. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this unit commander. I wouldn't have been such a unit commander. It's obvious that he has taken up this right that is not his. I don't know on the basis of what had this gentleman drafted the document. Also, the stamp verifying the document, authorising the document, is illegal, because on the 12th of May, VRS was established, and stamps of the VRS were the only legitimate stamps. We can see here that the stamp of the command of the 19th Partisan Brigade, and the SFRY coat of arms. I cannot comment this document because this seems like an improvisation to me. I wouldn't have drafted it this way, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that this order, at least based on what's in the document, this order has -- has its effect of establishing the entire authorities of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on this document. I haven't drafted it. I haven't ordered anyone to draft it. During the proofing when I was shown this document, there was a confusion about the term "Vakuf." There was confusion between Skender Vakuf and Donji Vakuf. The two towns are 150 kilometres away from each other. But, no, I cannot comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let us --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just for one moment -- would Your Honours hear me for one moment. Your Honours, I'm a little bit concerned about this question of being shown things by proofing which either not been shown or shown them. This document was not shown to this witness during any proofing. It is not part of any of our documents. It may have been shown to him at an earlier stage, when he was interviewed. But it certainly wasn't shown to him during proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only asked this witness on the basis of his claim that he was shown the document during his contacts with the Prosecution. I have no position on that. I heard him say that, and I spoke about the document in such a way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about discussions relating to disarmament of the Muslim formations in Vecici on their departure from the area, after they have done that and so on. Have the Muslim and Croat formations eventually handed over their weapons and left the area?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you about a telegram relating to events that took place at Koricanske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P609 put up on the screen. I apologise, I was looking for a different document, it seems. Just a moment, Your Honours, please. When the witness was discussing the telegram, I noted down this number, 609, but it seems that it's a different document that I'm looking for. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I sent it to two different addressees, to the corps, but also to the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you have no knowledge of whether the CSB received your telegram or was it informed by the corps?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't get any reply to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't have any contacts with the CSB in relation to this event. Isn't that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). I went to the site on the very same day, when I -- I was, that day, in Banja Luka, at the briefing, and at about 2300 hours, roughly, I went to the site where I couldn't see very much, but one could smell the smells coming from the abyss, and I could also see on the location there traces of blood, bullet casings, and I went back to the command --

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you yourself and those who were with you and went down there to get a closer look did not observe any bodies of women or children among them, did you?

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one thing that I have to explain. At one point, I noticed a group of civilians approaching the victims. They were civilians from a nearby village who wanted to see if there were any valuables to be had. They started rummaging through the pockets of the victims. I called to them, standing on the top of the ridge, shooing them away, in fact. But they were nearby locals. They were not connected to the individuals who were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely my point. It's not that there were bodies of women and children among the dead men there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The platoon of scouts did not come across any women or children. Instead, they found six seriously wounded individuals who were evacuated by the medical corps to the medical station in Knezevo. Therefore, neither the scouts who conducted the search, nor the medical team which evacuated the wounded, noticed or observed anyone else than the six wounded who were taken care of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ST-197 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness. Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You were at the scene the day itself or the day after the massacre happened, right? And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And you said first time you were there you couldn't see much but you could smell what was coming from down the -- the cliff. You, as a military man, must have seen and -- and been in the presence of dead men on other occasions. Is -- is there a smell coming from dead bodies that fresh? Was that the smell of rotting bodies, and could that happen in so -- so little time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, as a soldier, I have to tell you that I experienced all sorts of odours in my time, and I can recognise them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I will now be changing topics. Yesterday, in answer to the Prosecutor's question about your --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, can we go to a private session. [Microphone not activated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What the Chamber suggests is the following. That we will adjourn now and we will then allow the time to the parties that they need to sort this out. 30 minutes is -- is perhaps not long enough for you to reach some sort of an agreement. So if you want to take 40 or even 45 minutes, then feel free to do so. The Chamber is minded to give off Tuesday as well, if -- if there is any possibility that by the end of Tuesday some sort of agreement can be reached about this. Obviously if the Defence will say that you need more time than Tuesday, that it will not be possible for you to reach an agreement by Tuesday, then we'll have to consider perhaps also taking Wednesday --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're just going to go ahead. If we haven't been told on Tuesday, we'll just go ahead and call the witnesses, and that's an end to it. Can I just raise one question. Your Honours, it is also important to know because the witness who is due to start some time tomorrow, but there's lengthy examination-in-chief and equally lengthy cross, so he is likely to go over to -- not to Friday but to next week, because tomorrow is Thursday, and this witness is going to go into tomorrow, clearly. So what we will say is, if -- so we raise it now, that he is allowed to go back home between Friday and -- if we adjourn on the Tuesday as well and come back on the Wednesday. Because I think it would be a bit much to keep -- not to mention the expense to keep him here between Friday and Wednesday even though is he in the middle of examination or cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now and ask the parties to let us know as soon as you have come to some sort of a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the discussions in the extended break have proved to a certain extent productive. The Defence would like to have not only Tuesday but Wednesday off. With one caveat and some reluctance the Prosecution is prepared to agree, subject, of course, to Your Honours' agreement, on the basis that we get by Wednesday the definitive and final answer on what the Defence are prepared to stipulate to in respect of adjudicated facts. The caveat we have is this. That with respect of the witnesses lined up for next week, the three witnesses who relate to adjudicated facts, the Defence must tell us by the close of the court's sitting this Friday, because Monday is a holiday and we have no opportunity otherwise to tell VWS to stand people down if that's what's required, as to whether the adjudicated facts to which these witnesses are going speak will be stipulated to. So, the three witnesses are ST-225, ST-050, ST-241. Notification by Friday, close of court's sitting, so quarter to 2.00, whether the adjudicated facts to which they will speak will be stipulated to. As regards the rest, Your Honours, with some hesitation, we will accede to, as I say, if Your Honours agree to having Wednesday off, provided that's it and we do finally get the definitive answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. On the face of it, Ms. Korner's request does not seem unreasonable. Does that present -- does Friday, close of business, present an insurmountable problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it doesn't, because we have agreed with Ms. Korner. We understand the situation the OTP is finding themselves concerning the witnesses for the next week. So we agreed that we will provide the -- our answer for the three witnesses that have to come -- that are scheduled to come next week by Friday, end of the court sitting. And for the rest, for all others, for all other witnesses we agree that -- that we will provide our definitive answer by end of Wednesday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that this is the joint position of both Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the Chamber approves the joint proposal of counsel in that regard, and the -- the -- the two days next week will be used to finalise these matters. And we're grateful to counsel for the effort that they have put in to trying to arrive at a resolution of this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We are grateful to Your Honours for understanding. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one final thing. The filing that Your Honours ordered for the earlier agreement to adjudicated facts, we suggest, really, this is a Defence filing, because it's for them to say exactly what they agree. So, obviously we'll -- when they've filed their -- if -- their motion on that, then we'll accede to it. Or it can be a joint filing. But, in any event, we don't want to start writing things down, sending it back to the Defence who've decided what they'll accept, so they ought to file the basic motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the only thing that we need add to Ms. Korner's observation is that we suppose that it would be practical for the Defence to prepare the first draft and what we would expect to receive is a joint -- the product of your joint efforts. What we are trying to avoid is a back and forth between counsel in terms of what, in fact, is stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is Your Honour saying that we should wait now until -- so we shouldn't file this Friday but wait until everything else has been finished? Well, then you're going to have bits and pieces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, what we -- what we -- what is already in agreement would help us in preparing the outstanding motions, so that we can work on them on -- on -- on Tuesday and Wednesday when we are out of court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But none of what has already previously been agreed has any affect on any of the outstanding motions, at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The problem is we don't know what has been agreed, so -- so if you say -- if you say it has nothing to do with the outstanding motions, we take your word for it. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- it would be helpful if we could know --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- what --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honours, what we are simply saying is, we'll await the Defence list, and then we'll -- and we'll file a joint motion. Basically we're saying, we're sick to death of drafting motions. This is the Defence time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So could we have the blinds down so that the witness could be escorted back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we stopped when we were discussing the delegation arriving from Banja Luka. You said that they visited there to tour the corridor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Krgovic. I'm reminded by the Court Officer that we -- when we adjourned we were in private session. Should we remain so?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we go to private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I take my belongings? Is that business done or should I leave them here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I believe the Prosecution is through with them and they would return them to the Registry so they could be given back to you. I believe that's the position.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, they've been given back to him. They were given back this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I thought he meant the documents that we were dealing with yesterday. The -- your other belongings, because the courtroom is used for other purposes, the -- the Court Officers would assist you with them. The ushers would assist you with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. Before we rise there's the matter of 65 ter 10520 that was uploaded -- that had been marked for identification. It has, thanks to the OTP, now been -- since been uploaded and may -- the MFI qualification may be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We take the adjournment to 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of October, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
